edges.note: An actor is an active object with a mailbox: state owned by one execution context, invocations reified as queued messages; active object is the in-process realization of the actor style.
Decoupling invocation from execution puts callers and servants on different threads - a direct mechanism for processing requests concurrently.
Compiler-generated continuations let one thread interleave many in-flight operations - concurrency without thread-per-request.
Async functions are stackless coroutines: suspension at await points with compiler-managed state, restricted to the async/await protocol.

edges.cite: MDN, async functions reference: an async function returns a Promise, and await consumes promises/thenables
edges.note: The awaitable object is a future/promise; the two mechanisms form one model.

edges.cite: MDN, 'The event loop' + async function docs: awaited continuations are scheduled as microtasks on the event loop
edges.note: In JS/Python-asyncio the resumption of awaited code is driven by the event loop.
Correlating a completion with its initiating request via an opaque token is the in-process form of the correlation needed by system-scale async request-reply.

edges.cite: Garlan & Shaw, An Introduction to Software Architecture: interpreter style = interpretation engine + the pseudo-program (bytecode) it executes
edges.note: A bytecode VM is exactly the style's organization: engine, pseudo-program, and execution state.
Building the system atop an abstract instruction set interpreted at runtime is realized concretely by a bytecode VM.
The token threaded through the call graph is the standard mechanism by which a user- or system-issued cancel reaches a running operation at safe points.
Deadline-carrying tokens/contexts (Go context.WithDeadline, .NET CancelAfter) are the implementation vehicle for enforcing timing bounds on operations.

edges.cite: Enterprise Integration Patterns, Competing Consumers: multiple consumers on one point-to-point channel, each message to exactly one
edges.note: Same-name pair: the design-level mechanism is the EIP pattern the system-topology arch entry names.

edges.cite: Enterprise Integration Patterns, Competing Consumers (system-scale reading of the same pattern)
edges.note: Same mechanism read at deployed-service-instance scale.

edges.cite: Azure Architecture Center, Competing Consumers pattern - related patterns list Queue-Based Load Leveling
edges.note: Scaling the drain side of the leveling queue is done by adding competing consumers.
Classic realization: each filter is a coroutine yielding items downstream, giving incremental pipeline processing without threads (Conway's original coroutine use was a pipeline).
Cooperative suspension/resumption interleaves multiple activities on one thread - the lightweight form of introducing concurrency.
Speculatively optimizing VMs (JVM, V8) depend on deoptimization as the safety net that makes speculative JIT compilation sound; without it the managed-runtime style loses its performance model.
Deopt transfers a running activation back to the bytecode interpreter tier of the same VM.

The dispatch loop is the load-bearing runtime mechanism of implicit-invocation systems: announced events are delivered by the loop to registered handlers. (Closest node; a general event-driven-architecture style node is missing.)
The FQS main loop that dequeues and runs function pointers enqueued by ISRs is an event loop at whole-firmware scale.
The executor object is exactly where the scheduling policy for contended CPU (which thread, when, what order) is chosen and applied.

edges.cite: Java Concurrency in Practice (Goetz et al.), ch. 6: the Executor framework's standard implementations are thread pools
edges.note: Submission-side abstraction backed by a pooled-worker execution policy.
Padding removes needless cache-coherence traffic on hot shared data - efficiency of the memory system in critical areas.

edges.cite: LMAX Disruptor technical paper (Thompson et al.): ring-buffer sequence counters are cache-line padded to eliminate false sharing
edges.note: The style's single-threaded-processor-plus-ring-buffer throughput model depends on padded sequences.
A short cheap common-case path is the canonical way to cut per-event work while keeping the general slow path for rare cases.
Forking subtasks across worker threads and joining is a direct mechanism for parallel processing of divisible work.
The future is the in-process handle for an eventual result - the same accepted-now/result-later contract the arch pattern establishes over the network.

edges.cite: POSA2, Active Object: clients receive a future through which the servant's eventual result is obtained
edges.note: The pattern's structure names the future as its result-return participant.

edges.cite: Game Engine Architecture (Gregory), 'The Game Loop and Real-Time Simulation': the loop drives updates of all engine subsystems each frame
edges.note: The engine's runtime layering is animated by the game loop; it is the mechanism the whole architecture ticks on.
A game loop is the game-domain instance of the endless poll-update-service main loop as whole-program structure.

edges.cite: Game Programming Patterns (Nystrom), Game Loop chapter: contrasted with the blocking GUI event loop - the game loop processes input without waiting for it
edges.note: Nystrom's own comparison: same driver-loop family, opposite blocking discipline.
User-space threads are a mechanism for adding cheap concurrency (many more logical threads than OS threads).
Actor runtimes (BEAM processes, Akka dispatchers, Java Loom) rest on runtime-scheduled lightweight threads; millions of actors are only feasible in user space.

edges.cite: POSA2, Half-Sync/Half-Async: the same pattern, described from in-process mechanism to whole-system layering
edges.note: Same-name pair bridged: the design-level split is the mechanism of the system-scale layering.

edges.cite: POSA2, Half-Sync/Half-Async implementation: the asynchronous layer is commonly built with Reactor (or Proactor) event demultiplexing
edges.note: Reactor supplies the async-layer event dispatching.
A job system is an applied scheduling policy: dependency-DAG ordering of small tasks onto contended cores.

edges.cite: Game Engine Architecture (Gregory), concurrency chapter: modern engine runtimes decompose frame work into jobs run by the engine's job system
edges.note: The engine layers' per-frame work is executed through the job system.

edges.cite: Game Engine Architecture (Gregory): jobs are scheduled onto a fixed pool of worker threads (one per core)
edges.note: The job scheduler's execution substrate is a pinned worker pool.
A rotating thread set demultiplexing and processing events concurrently is a concurrency-introduction mechanism tuned to avoid hand-offs.
Pre-created processes/threads taking turns on accept() is the leader/followers protocol at server-architecture scale.

edges.cite: POSA2, Leader/Followers: consequences/see-also compare it with Half-Sync/Half-Async queue-based thread pooling
edges.note: Both structure concurrent event processing; L/F trades the queue layer away for lower latency.
Distributing independent loop iterations across threads is the most direct data-parallel form of introducing concurrency.

edges.cite: OpenMP execution model (spec) / Patterns for Parallel Programming (Mattson et al.): parallel loops execute under a fork-join model
edges.note: The parallel-for region forks a team and joins at the loop end.

edges.cite: POSA1, Master-Slave: fault-tolerance variant - slaves are replicas, the master compares/votes their results
edges.note: The pattern's fault-tolerance variant is a voting implementation.

edges.cite: Dean & Ghemawat, 'MapReduce' (OSDI 2004): one copy is the master, assigning map/reduce tasks to workers
edges.note: The MapReduce runtime is a master-worker structure at datacenter scale.
Superloops only stay responsive if every task is non-blocking; the one-short-step-per-invocation state-machine task is the mechanism that makes that possible.
Advancing one bounded step per scheduler pass places an explicit limit on execution time per invocation.
The no-OS cooperative loop forbids blocking waits, forcing long activities into stepwise state-machine form.
Hardware/NVIC interrupt priority preemption is the lowest-level implementation of servicing important events ahead of less important ones.
Event-triggered systems rely on interrupt-driven activation; nesting keeps high-priority event latency bounded under load.
The reduce phase is a distributed parallel reduction: tree/partial combination with an associative operator.
The tree of partial reductions is naturally expressed and scheduled as recursive fork-join tasks.

edges.cite: Garlan & Shaw, An Introduction to Software Architecture: filters compute incrementally and concurrently; pipelines are named as the linear specialization
edges.note: Threaded stages connected by queues are the concurrent execution of the pipes-and-filters style inside one system.
SEDA is stage-per-thread-pool pipeline parallelism promoted to whole-service structure; the stage/queue mechanism is what the style runs on.
Completion-dispatched asynchronous operations service many requests concurrently without dedicating a thread per request.

edges.cite: POSA2, Proactor: presented as the asynchronous counterpart of Reactor (readiness- vs completion-based demultiplexing)
edges.note: Same event-demux role, opposite I/O model.

edges.cite: POSA2, Proactor: uses Asynchronous Completion Token to demultiplex completion events to their handlers efficiently
edges.note: ACT is the pattern's completion-routing participant.
Protothreads give the superloop's event-driven C tasks a sequential blocking-style structure with two-byte state - purpose-built for OS-less main-loop firmware.

edges.cite: Dunkels et al., 'Protothreads' (SenSys 2006): described as an extremely lightweight stackless mechanism related to coroutines, built on local continuations
edges.note: A stackless C coroutine realization via switch-based local continuations.

Registered-handler dispatch from a synchronous demultiplexer is the concrete runtime of implicit-invocation organization for I/O-driven systems. (Closest node; general event-driven-architecture style missing.)
A reactor is an event loop specialized to OS-level I/O readiness demultiplexing (select/poll/epoll) with a handler-registration interface.
rseq removes atomic-instruction and lock overhead from per-CPU fast paths by letting the kernel restart interrupted critical sections.
rseq is the mechanism that makes per-CPU lock-free fast paths safe against migration/preemption.
An MPI-style SPMD program is a set of independent processes on multiple processors interacting by message passing - the distributed-processes style with one program text.

edges.cite: Patterns for Parallel Programming (Mattson et al.), Supporting Structures: SPMD, Master/Worker, Loop Parallelism and Fork/Join are presented as alternative parallel program structures
edges.note: Peer choices for structuring a parallel algorithm.
Neighborhood updates over a grid are embarrassingly parallel per generation; the stencil shape exists to expose that concurrency.
Distributed stencils are run SPMD: each rank owns a grid partition and exchanges halo/ghost cells with neighbors.
Confining task lifetimes to lexical scopes eliminates unconstrained parallelism (orphaned tasks, leaked threads) - directly the tactic's target.
A nursery/task-scope tree with error propagation and scope-wide cancellation is an in-process supervision tree; the structured-concurrency literature credits Erlang supervision as prior art.
The standard mechanism for processing different requests on different threads while bounding thread count.

edges.cite: Welsh, Culler & Brewer, 'SEDA' (SOSP 2001): each stage contains a thread pool managed by resource controllers
edges.note: Per-stage thread pools are the style's execution substrate.
Giving each thread its own copy of a logically global datum is replication to reduce contention - the tactic's stated purpose - applied at thread granularity.

edges.cite: Bell, 'Threaded Code' (CACM 1973): presented as an implementation technique for interpreted code representations
edges.note: A dispatch representation for the style's interpretation engine.
Direct/indirect threading is a standard dispatch technique inside bytecode VMs (e.g. gcc computed-goto interpreters).
Converting deep/mutual recursion into a constant-stack driver loop prevents stack-overflow failures from arising at all - the tactic's keep-exceptions-from-occurring intent.
Taking a component out of service in an orderly way depends on cooperative termination: request flag observed at safe points, then cleanup.

edges.cite: Candea & Fox, 'Crash-Only Software' (HotOS 2003): argues for crash+recover as the only stop/start path, explicitly against maintaining separate clean-shutdown code
edges.note: Cross-realm alternative: graceful two-phase shutdown vs designing so that crashing is the shutdown.

notes: All 37 g4 (execution-concurrency) elements bridged; unbridged list empty. Same-name pairs bridged: competing-consumers -> competing-consumers-system-topology/-scale (EIP), half-sync-half-async -> half-sync-half-async-system-layering (POSA2). One constrains example: superloop-architecture constrains multi-state-task. MISSING arch targets encountered: (1) a general event-driven-architecture style node (Richards/Fowler sense) - event-loop, reactor, async-await had to target event-based-implicit-invocation / function-queue-scheduling-architecture instead; (2) a master-worker / task-farm parallel style and a data-parallel/SPMD architecture node - parallel-programming elements (spmd, loop-parallelism, fork-join, parallel-reduction, stencil) funnel into introduce-concurrency, distributed-processes, mapreduce; (3) a managed-runtime / JIT-compilation platform node - deoptimization mapped to virtual-machine-architectural-style; (4) a graceful-shutdown / lifecycle-management concept - two-phase-termination mapped to removal-from-service; (5) concurrency-tactic vocabulary is thin (only introduce-concurrency + schedule-resources), causing many concurrency mechanisms to converge on introduce-concurrency.
